title: MultiPL-E: A Scalable and Extensible Approach to Benchmarking Neural Code Generation
review_status: full-text audit complete; benchmark translation, hidden-test protocol, language/prompt sensitivity, and transfer boundary checked
sections_checked: §6 translation choices, type annotations, prompt sensitivity, and error analysis

evidence_note: 18 additional languages; HumanEval and MBPP; Codex, CodeGen, InCoder; unit-test pass@1. MBPP assertions are hidden from prompts. Authors note benchmark tasks may not represent real language tasks, small prompt choices affect scores, and up to five HumanEval items require omission/modification for some target-language constraints. Results are conditional on translations, prompts, models, and tests.

title: Explaining the Contributing Factors for Vulnerability Detection in Machine Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; 17-project Java comparison, baseline, two cross-project protocols, and label/domain limitations checked
sections_checked: factor comparisons and reported random-forest baseline
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2024-06-05; no venue assertion made
evidence_note: Across 17 Java projects (15 Android), bag-of-words plus random forest is reported about 4 percentage points more accurate than other tested combinations. With a precision-and-recall threshold of 0.8, single-project training averages 1.4 target projects; 14-project training/testing on the held-out fifteenth reaches the threshold on 5/15. Authors note only Java, limited project count, and inherited static-analysis labels that may contain false positives. Cross-project transfer itself has prior literature.

title: DeepCodeProbe: Towards Understanding What Models Trained on Code Learn
review_status: full-text audit complete; probe construction, selected models/tasks, validation checks, and construct/external validity threats checked
sections_checked: four model/task families and syntax-derived probe construction
threats to construct, conclusion, and external validity
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2024-07-11; ACM manuscript available in arXiv record
evidence_note: Four non-transformer maintenance models across clone detection, summarization, and comment generation. Results support recoverable abstract syntax representations in these selected models; the paper explicitly notes probes can distort what models learned and that external validity is bounded by selected architectures/data availability. Probe performance is not a direct measure of functional correctness or safety.
